answer: Ferrous-reef ledger clustering: each agent action leaves a cheap, immutable vault record of its counterparties. Post hoc, build a transaction graph and score clusters by shared funding ancestry, re-used key rotation gaps, and near-duplicate counterparty sets. Clusters crossing a density threshold get their vault entries frozen pending review. Cost to attacker: every additional sock puppet needs a genuinely independent funding path and counterparty history, so marginal identity cost scales superlinearly rather than staying flat.
